arxiv-2106-12691.title: Damping of the Franz-Keldysh oscillations in the presence of disorder
arxiv-2106-12691.creator: R. E. Putnam, Jr. and M. E. Raikh
arxiv-2106-12691.description: Abstract Franz-Keldysh oscillations of the optical absorption in the presence of short-range disorder are studied theoretically. The magnitude of the effect depends on the relation between the mean-free path in a zero field and the distance between the turning points in electric field. Damping of the Franz-Keldysh oscillations by the disorder develops at high absorption frequency.

arxiv-2107-01931.title: Adiabatic Dynamical-Decoupling Based Control of Nuclear Spin Registers
arxiv-2107-01931.creator: O.T. Whaites, J. Randall, T.H. Taminiau, T.S. Monteiro
arxiv-2107-01931.description: Abstract The use of the nuclear spins surrounding electron spin qubits as quantum registers and long-lived memories opens the way to new applications in quantum information and biological sensing. Hence, there is a need for generic and robust forms of control of the nuclear registers.

arxiv-2107-04240.title: Deep Image Synthesis from Intuitive User Input: A Review and Perspectives
arxiv-2107-04240.creator: Yuan Xue, Yuan-Chen Guo, Han Zhang, Tao Xu, Song-Hai Zhang, Xiaolei Huang
arxiv-2107-04240.description: Abstract In many applications of computer graphics, art and design, it is desirable for a user to provide intuitive non-image input, such as text, sketch, stroke, graph or layout, and have a computer system automatically generate photo-realistic images that adhere to the input content.

arxiv-2301-07829.title: Warning: humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes
arxiv-2301-07829.creator: Kimberly T. Mai
arxiv-2301-07829.description: Abstract Abstract Speech deepfakes are artificial voices generated by machine learning models. Previous literature has highlighted deepfakes as one of the biggest security threats arising from progress in artificial intelligence due to their potential for misuse. However, studies investigating human detection capabilities are limited.

arxiv-2505-06730.title: Activity and Subject Detection for UCI HAR Dataset with & without missing Sensor Data
arxiv-2505-06730.creator: Debashish Saha, Piyush Malik, Adrika Saha
arxiv-2505-06730.description: Abstract Current studies in Human Activity Recognition (HAR) primarily focus on the classification of activities through sensor data, while there is not much emphasis placed on recognizing the individuals performing these activities. This type of classification is very important for developing personalized and context-sensitive applications.

arxiv-2506-06917.title: Graph-Based Physics-Guided Urban PM2.5 Air Quality Imputation with Constrained Monitoring Data DOI: 10.1145/3734869 CCS: Applied computing Environmental sciences CCS: Computing methodologies Spatial and physical reasoning CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning algorithms
arxiv-2506-06917.creator: Shangjie Du *, Hui Wei *, Dong Yoon Lee, Zhizhang Hu, Shijia Pan
arxiv-2506-06917.description: Abstract . This work introduces GraPhy , a graph-based, physics-guided learning framework for high-resolution and accurate air quality modeling in urban areas with limited monitoring data. Fine-grained air quality monitoring information is essential for reducing public exposure to pollutants. However, monitoring networks are often sparse in socioeconomically disadvantaged regions, limiting the accuracy and resolution of air quality modeling.

pmc-10667863.title: Successful Surgical Management of Ruptured Hepatic Artery Pseudoaneurysm Post-Liver Retransplant: A Case Report
pmc-10667863.creator: Seyed Mohammad Reza Nejatollahi, Arman Hasanzade, Fariba Ghorbani
pmc-10667863.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionHepatic Artery Pseudoaneurysm (HAP) is a rare and potentially fatal complication following liver transplantation, with unclear etiology. Various predisposing factors, including local infections, biliary-enteric anastomosis, particularly Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy, vascular interventions, and iatrogenic injuries, have been identified.Presentation of caseWe report a case of HAP occurring after liver re-transplantation in a twenty-year-old male patient who had initially undergone liver transplantation for cirrhosis resulting from autoimmune hepatitis.

pmc-11430723.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Tympanomastoid Paragangliomas: A Report from Slovenia
pmc-11430723.creator: Manja Hribar, Iztok Fošnarič, Aleš Matos, Robert Šifrer, Aleš Grošelj, Maruša Debeljak, Nina Zidar, Primož Strojan, Klemen Jenko
pmc-11430723.description: Simple SummaryTemporal bone paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors that typically arise from the parasympathetic nervous system. Since they are not a common pathology in the daily practice of an otorhinolaryngologist, we would like to provide an overview of current treatment strategies for patients with tympanomastoid paragangliomas.

pmc-11505377.title: Endothelial Biomarkers Are Superior to Classic Inflammatory Biomarkers in Community-Acquired Pneumonia
pmc-11505377.creator: Paula González-Jiménez, Mónica Piqueras, Ana Latorre, Jordi Tortosa-Carreres, Noé Mengot, Ricardo Alonso, Soledad Reyes, Isabel Amara-Elori, Luis Martínez-Dolz, Antonio Moscardó, Rosario Menéndez, Raúl Méndez, Galina F Sud’ina
pmc-11505377.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Complications in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), including cardiovascular events (CVE), can occur during an acute episode and in the long term. We aimed to analyse the role of endothelial damage biomarkers (C-terminal endothelin-1 precursor fragment [CT-proET-1] and mid-regional pro-adrenomedullin [MR-proADM]), in contrast to classic inflammation markers (C Reactive Protein [CRP] and procalcitonin [PCT]) in patients admitted for CAP and their relationship with ICU admission, CVE and mortality in the short and long term; Methods: Biomarkers were analysed in 515 patients with CAP

pmc-11618738.title: Enhanced Photothermal‐Assisted Hydrogen Production via a Porous Carbon@MoS2/ZnIn2S4 Type II‐S‐Scheme Tandem Heterostructure
pmc-11618738.creator: Ning Li, Yong Ma, Jiafeng Ma, Qing Chang, Xiangqian Fan, Lei Liu, Chaorui Xue, Caihong Hao, Huayang Zhang, Shengliang Hu, Shaobin Wang
pmc-11618738.description: MoS2/ZnIn2S4 flower‐like heterostructures into porous carbon (PC@MoS2/ZIS) are embedded. This ternary heterostructure demonstrates enhanced light absorption across a broad spectral range from 200 to 2500 nm. It features both Type‐II and S‐scheme dual heterojunction interfaces, which facilitate the generation, separation, and transfer of photoinduced carriers.

pmc-13522664.title: Efficacy and Safety of Celecoxib Combined with Gabapentin for Head and Facial Pain in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13522664.creator: Xiangrong Cao, Linzong Xu, Weiwei Ta
pmc-13522664.description: BackgroundHead and facial pain caused by local invasion in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is notoriously severe and traditionally managed with opioids, which carry substantial dependence and tolerability risks. Because this tumor-related pain intrinsically involves both neuropathic and inflammatory pathways, we retrospectively evaluated a novel opioid-sparing analgesic strategy combining celecoxib and gabapentin.

pmc-13530807.title: Poster 257. Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block with and without Liposomal Bupivacaine for Postoperative Pain Control in Total Shoulder Arthroplasty
pmc-13530807.creator: Heinz R. Hoenecke, Imran Gruhonjic, Jordan K. Penn, Matthew G. Hanley, Keith A. Alfieri
pmc-13530807.description: Objective:Interscalene brachial plexus nerve blocks are commonly used to reduce postoperative pain in patients undergoing shoulder surgery. Although effective, these blocks typically last 24 hours or less. Liposomal bupivacaine (LB) acts as a longer lasting amide anesthetic and may improve postoperative analgesia, however there is limited data regarding its use for total shoulder arthroplasty.
